note: The step half of CASE 2, and the reason `dead` must not be reseeded. This pair is the 44-minute gap of 2026-07-26 (quince-devlog#13): the last live tick was 09:56:16Z, a host-client reconnect at 09:58:38Z restarted the session process and dropped the pending wakeup, quince#36 and #37 opened into the gap, and the catch-up tick at 10:40:19Z reported them all at once. Because step() diffs against the STORED observation rather than against the world as it is at arm time, re-arming produces the events that accrued — not `queue-empty`, and not silence. A hand-rolled mitigation written during that same incident got this wrong in the opposite direction: it baselined against current heads when it armed, so both of the pushes it existed to catch were already inside its baseline.
